table.name: TLGNC_SHIPPINGPOINT_LOADTARGET
table.description: Expected load target information for a Material and Shippingpoint. Relevant for rail shippingpoints (wagons, maybe containers), but it could be used also for trucks: An entry defines how many loads (wagon, container,...) of a certain material are expected to be loaded per day at a shippingpoint. If no orders exist to be loaded, the system will consult this table and determine what pre-loading order could be created. If the number of loads loaded today (preloaded incl. used for customer orders) is reached, no pre-loading will happen anymore. The target_load_count can be exceeded but only by custom-orders, not with pre-loading orders.

column.name: SHIPPINGPOINT_ID
column.description: FK tlgnc_shippingpoint. Shippingpoint where this load target should the reached daily. Note, this is NOT the SAP Shippingpoint Number, but the technical ID of that shippingpoint in Logon DB.

column.name: SAP_MATERIAL_ID
column.description: FK tlgns_sap_material. Material (Product) of this load target. Note, this is NOT the SAP Material Number, but the technical ID of that material in Logon DB. (shippingpoint_id, sap_material_id, production_plant_cd, shippingpointpoin_id) is the business identifier for a record of this table, and must be unique.

column.name: PRODUCTION_PLANT_CD
column.description: Production Plant where the material is produced. In most cases this will be identical to tlgnc_shippingpoing.plant_cd (the supply plant), but it must be possible to express load targets for materials originally produced somewhere else.

column.name: TARGET_LOAD_COUNT
column.description: Targeted number of loads defined by (load_quantity, load_uom_cd) of this material at the shippingpoint_id.

column.name: LOAD_UOM_CD
column.description: FK tlgnr_uom_bs. Unit of measure on which LOAD_QUANTITY is based. This can be a real UOM such as 'TO', but also a 'fuzzy' UOM such as 'LKW' (a full truck), 'CON' (container), 'BW' (wagon).

column.name: LOAD_QUANTITY
column.description: Quantity of the material in units defined by LOAD_UOM_CD. Typical examples: 1 BW (for direct rail pre-loading), 54 TO (for Bimodal pre-loading).

column.name: PRELOAD_COMMENT
column.description: Comment which will be sent to the weighing system (Parallel) in parameter orderComment when creating a pre-load order.
